samples.summary: `selection.rawAnchor` is never invalidated, so shift+click extends from a stale mousedown anchor after any non-pointer caret change
samples.evidence: Shift+click now resolves its anchor as `this.selection.rawAnchor ?? this.selection.range?.anchor ?? this.cursor.position` (line 2073, and the cell variant at line 2007). `rawAnchor` is only ever written in the pointerdown handler (lines 1990, 2001, 2018, 2028, 2042, 2057, 2067, 2074, 2081) — grep for `.rawAnchor` finds no other writer. `Selection.setRange()` (selection.ts) does not touch it, and none of the ~40 `selection.setRange(null)` / `setRange(...)` call sites do either: arrow keys (text-editor.ts:3232, 3274, 3277), typing, select-all, find/replace, `restoreLocalCursor` (editor.ts:4317) and `resetAfterDocumentReplace` (editor.ts:4345) all leave the old click position in `rawAnchor`. Concrete regression: click at offset 5, press Right three times (selection cleared, caret at 8), then shift+click at 20 — the old code anchored at `cursor.position` (8) and selected 8..20; the new code anchors at the stale `rawAnchor` (5) and selects 5..20. Same after typing, after Ctrl+A (anchor should be doc start, becomes the old click), and after switching edit context header→body (anchor points into a block of the other region, which `normalizeRange` then rejects). A wrong selection is then acted on by delete/paste/style.

samples.summary: `snapRangeForLinks` substitutes `rawAnchor` for the anchor on *every* drag move, undoing the deliberate table-exit anchor rewrite and breaking drag-selection out of a table cell
samples.evidence: `snapRangeForLinks` builds `fromRaw = raw ? { ...range, anchor: raw } : range` (line 2379) and `expandRangeForLinks` returns that same object when nothing is expanded (link-run.ts:143 and :152), so the raw anchor replaces the caller's anchor even when no link is involved. In `updateDragSelection`, when the pointer leaves the table the code deliberately drops the cell-level anchor: `setRange({ anchor: { blockId: tableBlockId, offset: 0 }, focus: pos })` (lines 2352-2355, 'so buildRects treats the table as a whole-block highlight'). On the next mousemove `anchor = this.selection.range.anchor` is that table block, `getCellInfo(tableBlockId)` is undefined for a top-level table (getCellInfo → blockParentMap, line 3613), so control reaches line 2362 and `snapRangeForLinks` puts the original *cell* block back as the anchor. `normalizeRange` returns null for a cell anchor with a non-cell focus ('Mixed or cross-cell — no valid selection', selection.ts:153-171), so from the second mousemove onward the drag has no usable selection: no highlight, copy returns '', delete is a no-op.

samples.summary: The new Apply guard only checks that *some* link is at the caret, so it can rewrite a different link than the one being edited
samples.evidence: `if (editingExistingLink && !editor.getLinkAtCursor()) { … return; }` (line 152) tests only truthiness, not identity with the link the popover was opened on. The popover deliberately stays open when the caret leaves the link (lines 69-76), so the user can click into a *different* hyperlink and press Apply: `getLinkAtCursor()` is truthy, the guard passes, and `insertLink(url)` takes the caret in-place branch (editor.ts:3619) and rewrites that unrelated link's href — and now, with this change, also its display text when it is self-labelled (editor.ts:3641-3661). Similarly, if the user drags a new selection whose focus lands in any link, the guard passes and `insertLink` takes the `hasSelection()` branch (editor.ts:3582), applying the href to the whole new selection. Comparing against the href/run the popover was editing (or against `linkInfo.href` / the original position) is what the guard needs.

samples.summary: `rawAnchor` can name a block that no longer exists, yielding a selection every consumer silently rejects
samples.evidence: `rawAnchor` is a plain position captured at mousedown (line 2081) and is never cleared when the document changes: `resetAfterDocumentReplace` (editor.ts:4325-4347) clears the selection and cursor but not `rawAnchor`, and merging/deleting the clicked block (backspace at offset 0) removes the block it names. A later shift+click then builds `{ anchor: <dead blockId>, focus: pos }`; `normalizeRange` returns null when the anchor block is not in the layout (selection.ts:152), so the shift+click appears to do nothing (no highlight, empty copy, delete no-op) instead of extending from the live caret as before.

samples.summary: The in-place URL rewrite moves the caret without requesting scroll-into-view
samples.evidence: The plain caret-insert branch sets `needsScrollIntoView = true` before `render()` (line 3681), but the new rewrite branch moves the caret to `link.start + url.length` (line 3660) after replacing the run's text — which can be much longer than the old URL and can push the caret off-screen or onto a new wrapped line — and calls `render()` (line 3665) without `needsScrollIntoView`. The caret can end up outside the viewport.

samples.summary: The replacement text inherits only the link's last sub-run style, silently flattening mixed formatting (and any commentId) across the rewritten run
samples.evidence: `doc.insertText({ offset: link.end }, url)` puts the whole new URL inside the link's *last* inline (resolveOffset returns the preceding inline at a boundary, block-helpers.ts:34), then the original text 0..link.end-link.start is deleted. For a link split into same-href sub-runs — exactly the case the new test 'rewrites the URL text of a link that carries styled sub-runs' constructs (bold prefix) — every style other than href is replaced by the last sub-run's style: the bold prefix is lost, and any other per-run style (color, fontSize, or a `commentId` carried by that last inline) is applied to the entire replacement. The test only asserts text and href, so this is unobserved.

samples.summary: After link expansion the caret is moved to a new offset while carrying the pre-expansion line affinity
samples.evidence: `withOffset` deliberately drops `lineAffinity` when it moves an endpoint (link-run.ts:109-112), but the callers then re-supply the *old* hit's affinity: `this.cursor.moveTo(snapped.focus, snapped.focus.lineAffinity ?? result.lineAffinity)` (line 2365, and 2023/2077). When the expansion moves the focus across a visual wrap boundary, the affinity from the un-expanded position is wrong for the new offset, so the caret and the selection highlight can paint on the previous line — the exact failure mode the affinity plumbing exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: shift+click resolves its anchor as `this.selection.rawAnchor ?? this.selection.range?.anchor ?? this.cursor.position` (text-editor.ts:2072-2073, cell variant 2006-2007). A repo-wide grep shows `rawAnchor` is written only inside `handleMouseDown` (1990, 2001, 2018, 2028, 2042, 2057, 2067, 2074, 2081); `Selection.setRange()` assigns only `this.range` (selection.ts:704-706), and the `Selection` instance is long-lived (constructed at editor.ts:1106, injected at text-editor.ts:698). Non-pointer caret changes clear the range but leave `rawAnchor` stale — e.g. plain arrow keys at text-editor.ts:3232, 3274, 3277 and Home/End non-shift branches (3299). So after click → arrow key, a shift+click anchors at the old mousedown position instead of the current caret, yielding a wrong selection that delete/paste/style then act on; in the cell path the stale anchor's cell identity (2008-2011) can also wrongly collapse the selection. Reachable in ordinary use; not guarded anywhere. Major severity is appropriate (wrong behavior/state on a normal path).

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out. snapRangeForLinks (text-editor.ts:2377-2381) unconditionally substitutes selection.rawAnchor for the caller's anchor, and expandRangeForLinks returns that same object on its no-op paths (link-run.ts:143, :152; anchorComesFirst yields undefined for cell blocks because doc.getBlockIndex doesn't index non-top-level blocks, link-run.ts:102-105). The table-exit branch (text-editor.ts:2348-2359) deliberately rewrites the anchor to the table block and returns early without clearing rawAnchor, which still holds the mousedown cell position (set at :2042; none of the rawAnchor=null sites at :1990/:2001/:2028/:2057/:2067 are on this path), and setRange stores the range verbatim (selection.ts:704-706). On the following mousemove, anchor is the table block, getCellInfo is a bare blockParentMap.get (text-editor.ts:3609-3613) which lacks top-level table blocks, so anchorCellInfo is undefined and control falls to :2362 where the cell anchor is restored. normalizeRange then returns null for a cell anchor with a non-cell focus (selection.ts:153-171), so getNormalizedRange/getSelectedText yield null/'' (selection.ts:722-741) and the highlight is empty — the drag has no usable selection from the second mousemove onward. Reachable in normal drag-out-of-table use; no guard makes it unreachable.

finding.summary: The new Apply guard only checks that *some* link is at the caret, so it can rewrite a different link than the one being edited
finding.evidence: `if (editingExistingLink && !editor.getLinkAtCursor()) { … return; }` (line 152) tests only truthiness, not identity with the link the popover was opened on. The popover deliberately stays open when the caret leaves the link (lines 69-76), so the user can click into a *different* hyperlink and press Apply: `getLinkAtCursor()` is truthy, the guard passes, and `insertLink(url)` takes the caret in-place branch (editor.ts:3619) and rewrites that unrelated link's href — and now, with this change, also its display text when it is self-labelled (editor.ts:3641-3661). verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. docs-link-popover.tsx:152 guards Apply with `editingExistingLink && !editor.getLinkAtCursor()` — a truthiness test only, with no comparison against the link the popover was opened on (available as linkInfo.href / editPosition, captured at lines 127-134). The popover genuinely stays in edit mode when the caret moves: onCursorLinkChange (lines 63-77) preserves mode === "edit" and merely retargets linkInfo, and no click-outside/blur handler closes it (docs-view.tsx:630-635 passes only editRequest/onEditRequestHandled/readOnly; the popover's onMouseDown only stops propagation for clicks inside itself, so canvas clicks move the caret). onCursorLinkChange is caret-driven via getLinkAtCursorPosition() in afterCursorRender (editor.ts:2402-2431), so the caret can land in an unrelated link with the popover still open and the stale URL in the input. Apply then passes the guard and insertLink resolves its target from the CURRENT caret (editor.ts:3617-3619, findLinkRunAt(block, pos.offset)), rewriting that unrelated link's href (3642) and — new in this change — its display text when self-labelled (3634, 3641-3661), also moving the caret (3660). The selection branch (3582-3607) likewise stamps the href across a fresh drag-selection whose focus happens to sit in a link. This is silent modification/destruction of untargeted document content on a normally reachable path: real, in the correctness lane, and blocking (major).
